name: Threading & Mutexes
essence: The lock that protects you from a race is the lock that deadlocks you.

examples.summary: Two transfers lock the same accounts in opposite order and deadlock.
examples.observed_output: fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!

examples.summary: `Withdraw` holds the mutex and calls `Balance`, which locks it again.
examples.observed_output: fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!

examples.summary: The sold-out early return leaves the mutex locked; the next caller deadlocks.
examples.mechanism: Unlock not deferred; error path skips release (CWE-667).
examples.observed_output:
guest 1: <nil>
guest 2: <nil>
guest 3: sold out
fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!

examples.summary: Value receiver copies the struct including its mutex, so each call locks a private copy while the shared map races.
examples.mechanism: Copied sync.Mutex protects nothing (go vet copylocks).

examples.summary: A reader holding RLock calls a method that RLocks again; a pending writer blocks the nested RLock.
examples.mechanism: RWMutex forbids recursive read locking once a writer is waiting.
examples.observed_output: fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!

examples.summary: Two threads lock the same mutexes in opposite order and block forever.
`take` holds the stock guard and calls `available`, which locks the same mutex.
examples.mechanism: std Mutex is not reentrant; relocking on the same thread deadlocks.

examples.summary: The guard from `queue.lock()` in the match scrutinee lives for the whole match, so the arm's second lock deadlocks.
examples.mechanism: Temporaries in a match scrutinee are dropped at the end of the match.

examples.summary: The validation throw happens after acquire and before release, so the lock is held forever.
examples.observed_output:
rejected: negative amount
next entry still waiting for the ledger lock after 200ms

examples.summary: Sale and refund acquire two async locks in opposite order across an await and deadlock.
examples.mechanism: Lock-order inversion works the same with promises as with threads.
examples.observed_output: sale and refund still blocked after 200ms

examples.summary: Each thread holds the lock the other needs, and both print blocked.
examples.mechanism: One thread acquires a then b. The other acquires b then a. Neither can take its second lock.

examples.summary: The same thread acquires the lock twice and the second acquire prints blocked.
examples.mechanism: threading.Lock is not reentrant. The owner blocks on a second acquire.

examples.summary: The error path never reaches release, so a later acquire prints blocked.
examples.mechanism: release sits after the raise. The except clause swallows the error and leaves the lock held.

examples.summary: outer holds the lock and calls inner, which needs the same lock, so inner prints blocked.
examples.mechanism: Lock does not count re-entry. The nested method cannot acquire the lock the caller still holds.
